chunks: And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean if God made the disbelievers hear but they still turned away?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the interplay between divine omniscience and human free will, suggesting that the 'good' (khayr) refers to the potential for accepting guidance, which was absent in the disbelievers' hearts. It underscores the concept of *tawallu* (turning away) as a conscious choice resulting from their inherent stubbornness, a theme frequently elaborated upon by scholars like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Kulayni in their discussions on the seal of closure for those who persist in disbelief.
